tie_reference: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.
source_note: Verified Physics Form One lesson plans (Arusha Catholic Seminary). 24 lesson plans (80 min double periods, 2 per week) covering Mechanical Properties of Matter (Weeks 1-3), Pressure (Weeks 4-6), Linear Motion (Weeks 7-9), and Work, Energy, and Power (Weeks 11-13) for Term II. Week 10 is mid-term assessment; Week 14 is annual examinations/closing of the academic year.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 14A (TERM II - WEEK 1, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF ELASTICITY
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Examine elastic and plastic behavior of materials using Hooke's Law
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Stretches a rubber band and a piece of clay, asking students to compare what happens when released.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe and compare the two materials' behavior.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains in depth elastic vs. plastic behavior and states Hooke's Law (extension proportional to force) with a worked example.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on elasticity and Hooke's Law.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical loading a spring with increasing weights, measuring extension, and plotting a force-extension graph.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform spring-loading practical and plot graph in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group graphs and administers a practical test on identifying the elastic limit.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 14B (TERM II - WEEK 1, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF ELASTICITY (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Interpret force-extension graphs and identify the elastic limit
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the graph plotted in the double period.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall the shape of the graph.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains in depth how to read a force-extension graph and identify the elastic limit point where the line stops being straight.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow the worked example.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides individual practice interpreting sample force-extension graphs and identifying elastic limits.
Reviews answers with the class and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 15A (TERM II - WEEK 2, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): ADHESION AND COHESION
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish adhesive and cohesive forces using capillary tube and liquid drop observations
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Capillary tubes, glass surfaces, water, oil.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Places a water drop on glass and asks students why it spreads or beads up.
Explains in depth adhesion (attraction between different molecules) and cohesion (attraction between like molecules) with examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes with labeled examples.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct differentiation of adhesion and cohesion

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical comparing water and oil drops on different surfaces to identify which forces dominate.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Test drops on surfaces in groups and record observations.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group findings and consolidates on the board.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 15B (TERM II - WEEK 2, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): ADHESION AND COHESION (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Identify real-life examples of adhesion and cohesion
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Example picture cards (paint, ink, waterproof fabric).
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the drop tests from the double period.
Explains in depth real-life applications where adhesion or cohesion dominates (paint sticking to walls, waterproof coatings).
Guides group activity classifying picture cards as examples of adhesion or cohesion.
Administers oral questions to check understanding.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 16A (TERM II - WEEK 3, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): SURFACE TENSION AND CAPILLARITY
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Examine surface tension using a floating needle and capillarity using tubes of different diameters
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Needles, water, capillary tubes of varying diameter.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students how a small insect can walk on water without sinking.
Explains in depth surface tension as a result of cohesive forces at a liquid's surface, and capillarity as liquid rise in narrow tubes.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on both concepts.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct explanation of surface tension and capillarity

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical floating a needle on water and observing capillary rise in tubes of different diameters.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform both practicals in groups and record results.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group results and consolidates the relationship between tube diameter and capillary rise.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 16B (TERM II - WEEK 3, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): SURFACE TENSION AND CAPILLARITY (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Identify real-life applications of capillarity (plants, ink pens, towels)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the capillary rise results from the double period.
Explains in depth real-life applications of capillarity (water rising in plant stems, ink moving up a pen, towels absorbing water).
Guides group discussion connecting each application to the capillarity principle learned.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Discuss and connect applications in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers a written short test on surface tension and capillarity.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 17A (TERM II - WEEK 4, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): PRESSURE DUE TO SOLIDS
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Examine the concept of pressure and calculate pressure exerted by solids
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Blocks of varying base area, sand tray, weights.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students why a sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt one with the same force.
Explains in depth the concept of pressure (force per unit area) and derives the formula with worked examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of the pressure formula

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical pressing blocks of different base areas into a sand tray, comparing the depth of impression.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform sand-tray practical in groups and record results.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group results and administers a calculation test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 17B (TERM II - WEEK 4, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): PRESSURE DUE TO SOLIDS (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Identify real-life applications of increasing/decreasing pressure (skis, sharp blades, wide tires)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the sand-tray results from the double period.
Explains in depth real-life applications where pressure is increased (nails, blades) or decreased (skis, wide tires, foundations).
Guides group activity classifying picture cards as increasing or decreasing pressure design.
Reviews classifications and administers oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 18A (TERM II - WEEK 5, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): PRESSURE IN LIQUIDS
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Examine factors affecting liquid pressure (depth, density) using a pressure apparatus
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Liquid pressure apparatus, measuring cylinders, liquids of varying density.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students why divers feel more pressure the deeper they swim.
Explains in depth factors affecting liquid pressure (depth and density) and derives the formula P = rho g h with a worked example.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow the worked example.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of liquid pressure formula

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical using a liquid pressure apparatus to measure pressure at different depths and with different liquids.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform pressure apparatus practical in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group results and administers a written short test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 18B (TERM II - WEEK 5, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): PRESSURE IN LIQUIDS (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Solve calculation problems using the liquid pressure formula
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the pressure formula from the double period.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall the formula P = rho g h.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Works through additional numerical problems calculating liquid pressure at various depths and densities.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Supervises individual practice solving liquid pressure calculation problems.
Marks sample answers on the board and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 19A (TERM II - WEEK 6, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Examine evidence for atmospheric pressure and its measurement using a barometer
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Simple barometer, tin can, heat source.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students if air has weight and can exert pressure, even though it's invisible.
Explains in depth the concept of atmospheric pressure and how it's caused by the weight of the air column above us.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on atmospheric pressure theory.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct explanation of atmospheric pressure cause

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Demonstrates the collapsing-can experiment (heating a can, sealing it, then cooling to show implosion from atmospheric pressure).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration and record explanation in groups.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct explanation of the observed collapse

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a barometer reading practical and administers a practical quiz.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Read barometer values and complete practical quiz.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 19B (TERM II - WEEK 6, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Explain how a drinking straw and a syringe use atmospheric pressure
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the collapsing-can demonstration from the double period.
Explains in depth how drinking straws and syringes work by creating a pressure difference using atmospheric pressure.
Guides group practical using straws and syringes to draw up water, discussing the pressure difference created.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Test straws/syringes in groups and discuss findings.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers a written test on atmospheric pressure applications.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 20A (TERM II - WEEK 7, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): MOTION, DISTANCE, AND DISPLACEMENT
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish distance from displacement using practical examples
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks a student to walk a zigzag path back to a nearby point and asks how far they walked vs. how far they ended up from the start.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe the walk and share observations.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains in depth the difference between distance (scalar, total path) and displacement (vector, straight-line change in position).
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct differentiation of distance and displacement

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical where students walk different paths and measure both distance traveled and displacement achieved.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform walking practical and measure both quantities in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group results and consolidates the vector vs. scalar distinction on the board.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 20B (TERM II - WEEK 7, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): MOTION, DISTANCE, AND DISPLACEMENT (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Solve problems distinguishing distance and displacement from given diagrams
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the walking practical results from the double period.
Works through diagram-based problems, guiding students to calculate distance and displacement from given paths.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Supervises individual practice solving distance/displacement problems from diagrams.
Reviews answers with the class and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 21A (TERM II - WEEK 8, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): SPEED, VELOCITY, AND ACCELERATION
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Calculate speed, velocity, and acceleration from given motion data
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students what it means when a car's speedometer changes from 40 km/h to 60 km/h.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share initial ideas about changing speed.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains in depth speed, velocity, and acceleration with formulas and derives each with worked examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of the three formulas

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical timing a rolling ball/trolley over a measured distance to calculate speed, then repeating with changing speed to find acceleration.
Reviews group results and administers a calculation test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 21B (TERM II - WEEK 8, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): SPEED, VELOCITY, AND ACCELERATION (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Interpret distance-time and speed-time graphs
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the calculations made in the double period.
Explains in depth how to read distance-time and speed-time graphs, including what the gradient represents.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides individual practice interpreting sample graphs and answering related questions.
Reviews answers with the class and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 22A (TERM II - WEEK 9, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): EQUATIONS OF LINEAR MOTION AND MOTION UNDER GRAVITY
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_competence: 8.3 Apply equations of linear motion and motion under gravity
lessons.specific_activity: Apply the equations of linear motion to solve problems including motion under gravity
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Drops a small ball and asks students what happens to its speed as it falls.
Explains in depth the equations of linear motion (v=u+at, s=ut+0.5at^2, v^2=u^2+2as) and applies them to motion under gravity (g=9.8 m/s^2).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical timing a free-falling object over a measured height to estimate g.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform free-fall timing practical in groups.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Accuracy of experimental estimate of g

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group results and administers a written test applying the motion equations.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 22B (TERM II - WEEK 9, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): EQUATIONS OF LINEAR MOTION AND MOTION UNDER GRAVITY (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_competence: 8.3 Apply equations of linear motion and motion under gravity
lessons.specific_activity: Additional problem-solving practice using the equations of motion
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the three equations of motion from the double period.
Works through additional numerical problems combining the equations with motion under gravity scenarios.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Supervises individual practice solving additional motion equation problems.
Marks sample answers on the board and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 23A (TERM II - WEEK 11, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF WORK
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Calculate work done using force and distance moved
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students if pushing a wall (that doesn't move) counts as doing work in the Physics sense.
Explains in depth the Physics definition of work (force multiplied by distance moved in the direction of force) with worked examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of the work formula

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group practical pulling a block a measured distance with a spring balance and calculating work done.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform pulling practical and calculate work in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group results and administers a calculation test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 23B (TERM II - WEEK 11, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF WORK (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Identify situations where work is or is not done in the Physics sense
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the work calculations from the double period.
Explains in depth scenarios where no work is done (holding a heavy bag still) vs. where work is done (carrying it up stairs).
Guides group activity classifying scenario cards as 'work done' or 'no work done'.
Reviews classifications and administers oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 24A (TERM II - WEEK 12, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF ENERGY
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Examine forms of energy and the principle of conservation of energy
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students to name different forms of energy they encounter daily (light, heat, sound, etc.).
Explains in depth different forms of energy (kinetic, potential, and others) and states the principle of conservation of energy.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on energy forms and conservation.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct explanation of energy forms and conservation

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Demonstrates a swinging pendulum, guiding groups to identify energy transformations (potential to kinetic) at different points of the swing.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe pendulum demonstration and identify energy changes in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group findings and administers a written short test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 24B (TERM II - WEEK 12, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF ENERGY (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Calculate kinetic and potential energy for given scenarios
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the pendulum energy transformations from the double period.
Explains in depth the formulas for kinetic energy (0.5mv^2) and potential energy (mgh) with worked examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Supervises individual practice calculating kinetic and potential energy for given scenarios.
Reviews answers with the class and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 25A (TERM II - WEEK 13, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF POWER
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_activity: Calculate power using work done and time taken
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students why two people carrying the same load up the same stairs, one running and one walking, both do the same work but not the same power.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share initial ideas about power vs. work.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains in depth power as the rate of doing work (Power = Work/Time) with the SI unit (Watt) and worked examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of the power formula

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides individual practice calculating power for various given work/time scenarios.
Marks sample answers on the board and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 25B (TERM II - WEEK 13, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): COMPREHENSIVE REVISION (CHAPTERS 6-9)
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of mechanical properties of matter, pressure, motion, and energy
lessons.specific_competence: 9.3 Explain the concept of power; comprehensive revision
lessons.specific_activity: Revise Chapters 6-9 and complete the revision test
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Outlines the topics covered in Chapters 6-9 (elasticity, adhesion/cohesion, surface tension, pressure, motion, work, energy, power).
Leads a rapid review of key Chapter 6-9 concepts through guided Q&A.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Answer questions and take additional notes.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Organizes a group quiz competition covering all four chapters.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Participation and accuracy in the competition

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers the comprehensive revision test and previews the annual examination.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Complete revision test; listen to exam preview.
